postgresSnapshot.readMethod: live SELECT of the restored registry row; state was parsed in-process and only bounded metadata was emitted

comparison.manifestComparison: restored state references were compared with the sourceKey, digest, and size fields in the earlier destination manifest

freshDestinationReadback.method: FilesSdkBlobStore.getVerified through createNodeFilesSdkBlobStore using files-sdk@2.4.0 and private Vercel Blob
freshDestinationReadback.credentialHandling: BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN was supplied to the targeted process by the Vercel CLI environment runner; its value was never printed or persisted

mutationBoundary.postgres: read-only SELECTs against the retained disposable target
mutationBoundary.blob: GET/head verification only through the Files SDK

coverage: The restored registry revision 232 references exactly the 11 source objects represented by the earlier Blob backup manifest, with matching keys, digests, and sizes.
Every existing destination-prefix object in that 11-object manifest was freshly downloaded and verified against its recorded digest and size.
The comparison covers the restored registry JSON state and the bounded non-CLI Blob manifest only; it is not a tenant-wide coordinated recovery proof.
limits: The PostgreSQL snapshot and the Blob copy were captured as separate operations; no shared MVCC/provider snapshot, quiescence fence, or coordinated freeze was established.
The restored state still names source sealed keys. The earlier copy maps those keys to a restore prefix; no application-level key remap, registry seed, or serving-path restore was run.

The source Blob inventory contained 14 objects; the bounded copy and fresh readback cover 11 non-CLI referenced objects totaling 37,741 bytes. Unreferenced/provider-side objects, versions, lifecycle rules, ACL/IAM, and hosted rollback remain unverified.

The PostgreSQL proof covers database-local schema and rows in its disposable target. Cluster-global roles/tablespaces, identity-provider credentials, billing-provider state, deployment values, and hosted application configuration remain outside this evidence.
No new Blob copy was performed during this verification.
